outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: The Challenge of Adapting Foundation Models
outline.description: The landscape of artificial intelligence has undergone a seismic shift in recent years, driven by the emergence of what are commonly referred to as large foundation models. These architectures, encompassing vast language models like ChatGPT and image generation systems such as Stable Diffusion, have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in generalization across diverse domains. Their success is not merely incremental; it represents a qualitative leap in performance that was previously thought to be unattainable by smaller models. This surge in capability is inextricably linked to the sheer scale of these models, which now contain billions, and in some cases hundreds of billions, of parameters. Cost Barriers to Training from Scratch

outline.description: As foundation models like ChatGPT and Stable Diffusion continue to dominate the landscape of artificial intelligence, the sheer scale of these architectures presents a formidable barrier to entry. Models such as GPT-3 contain approximately 175 billion parameters, rendering the cost of training such systems from scratch prohibitive for almost all researchers and practitioners. Consequently, the field has shifted its focus toward efficiently adapting these massive pre-trained models to specific downstream tasks without the luxury of full retraining. Within this realm of parameter-efficient finetuning (PEFT), three primary paradigms have emerged: model finetuning, adapter tuning, and prompt tuning. outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: An Information Transmission Framework for Matrix Factorization
outline.description: In the realm of modern deep learning, particularly when dealing with massive foundation models like large language models and vision transformers, the challenge of adapting these systems to downstream tasks without prohibitive computational costs has become paramount. While traditional parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods often rely on low-rank approximations or sparse additive updates, a more geometrically principled approach involves preserving the relational structure of the model's internal representations. One such method, Orthogonal Fine-tuning (OFT), posits that transforming neurons via orthogonal matrices can preserve pairwise angles between features, thereby retaining pre-trained knowledge.
